Task_Type.reason: Confirmed. This is a subtyping study of Parkinson's disease MCI (keyword 'Subtyping'; title 'A new subtype?'). 162 PD-MCI patients from PPMI are split by a -1 SD Ch4 grey-matter-density z-score into low (40) and normal (122) Ch4 groups. The groups are then compared on clinical scales (Kruskal-Wallis, chi-square) and on time to the first of six PPMI cognitive-domain milestones (Kaplan-Meier, log-rank P = 0.0017, Cox HR 1.75). The outcome is a composite (MoCA <21, MDS-UPDRS item 1.1 >=3, hallucinations, apathy, and two dementia definitions). It is not a progressive-vs-stable MCI label or MCI-to-AD conversion, and the main text reports no discrimination figure (no accuracy, AUC or sensitivity/specificity). The template allows T2 ONLY when the task is explicitly pMCI vs sMCI or MCI-to-AD conversion, so T2 is ruled out. A subtype-prognosis association is T4.
Task_Type.quote: Objective: To determine whether PD-MCI patients with MRI evidence of Ch4 degeneration exhibit a different clinical profile and cognitive trajectory than those without Ch4 degeneration.
